text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

---The controversy about the location of the new 750 million crown Royal Theatre rages on with the Liberals in Copenhagen City Council against a Norwegian architect's plan to incorporate a glass construction into the present opera-ballet-theatre complex in the city centre. Royal Theatre actors were not invited to participate in a public hearing on the new national theatre and pressure is mounting to locate the theatre in a site in Copenhagen not connected to the existing buildings.
--- 1996 was a good year for Danish companies with a decrease of more than 30 percent in the number of bankruptcies.

--- The Danish Consumer Council critises telecom group Tele Danmark for breaking marketing rules in its campaign for cheap overseas telephone calls, maintaining that consumers do not save the money claimed by the operator.
--- East Asiatic Company (EAC) has sold the last part of its shipping business to a Norwegian shipper and will now concentrate solely on sales of graphic equipment and foods.

--- Danish cleaning group ISS is now offering to run kindergartens for local authorities. ISS is mainly known for its cleaning services, but within the last six months the group has been looking into the possibility of diversifying into the childcare market.

--- Danish shipping group A.P. Moeller's Maersk Contractors unit and Danish environmental purification company Soil Recovery have started a joint venture cleaning polluted oil industry equipment worldwide.
